Therapist: Where would you like to start today?

Client: The same place as last week, I think. The evenings are still the hard part.

Therapist: Tell me about last night specifically.

Client: I got home about seven, and by half past I was going over the review meeting again. It was the same three sentences, over and over.

Therapist: What happened when you noticed you were doing it?

Client: Nothing at first. Then I got the notebook out and wrote it down, and it slowed a bit. Not gone, but slower.

Therapist: That is the second time this week the writing has helped. What would make it easier to reach for sooner?

Client: Keeping the notebook at work instead of in the hall. By the time I am home I have already had two hours of it.
